chapter_mission: A modern Jedi outpost near Veranthos — three young Knights, their Force contemplative practices failing as the Weave thins. Torin weaponises their suffering. Sera's moment of truth: rigid principle alone does not protect. Kael, watching the Knights, names the design problem — the resonance answer in embryonic form. Per W2 evidence-of-passage beat 2: Veraine has been here ahead of the group and left a short annotation in the outpost's archive; Ben finds it and registers her working mind against the same primary sources Kael is processing. Her wrongness is not ignorance — it is parallel reading of the same evidence.
chapter_turn: Three arcs hit their moment of truth in one chapter. Sera turns from Torin's framework to Ben's. Kael says more than he has said in days. Ben acquires the insight he does not yet recognise as the solution. The book's alternative answer is now in the room, spoken aloud by its most unexpected voice. Veraine's annotation in the archive shows Ben that she has sat with these same materials and reached her conclusion — and has moved on toward Veranthos while he reads.

scene_plan.purpose: The outpost reads normal from approach. The Knight who meets them at the pad does not — eyes too wide, hands too still. Ben and the group move through training halls where drills have been abandoned mid-exercise. A young Knight describes losing the ability to meditate: 'The Force is there but I can't find the shape of it anymore.' Ben recognises the description — the parallax error from the Battlefield Node, now permanent here. Torin kneels beside the Knight with a commander's hand on her shoulder; the tenderness is real, the eyes over her head are calculating. The outpost's senior — a disciplined man who has built forty years of identity on contemplative practice — cannot hold a basic centring exercise, and says so without apology. The Weave has thinned enough that a tradition whose whole technology is Weave-listening has gone silent.

Outpost common area. Torin uses the Knights' suffering as argument — these are proof the seal cannot be maintained incrementally. His compassion is genuine and his conclusion is the old one. Sera watches the exchange. Her rigid certainty has not protected these Knights. Ben's response to helplessness — honest, no false authority — shows her a kind of leadership Gavran never demonstrated. She turns away from Torin and faces Ben directly: 'What is your plan, Skywalker?' Not conditional. A genuine question. In the margin of the scene: Ben catches, in Sera's momentary silence before she speaks, the same not-said quality from Ch 18 — the lie_fissure widening without announcing itself.

Outpost exterior wall at the archive alcove. Kael leans with arms folded, watching the Knights through the open doorway. He speaks more than he has spoken in days — quiet, precise, the outsider naming what insiders cannot see: 'They built everything on one thing. Take it away and they don't know how to stand. That's not a Weave problem. That's a design problem.' He does not know what he has just said. Ben does not yet either. While Kael speaks, Ben is scrolling the outpost's historical archive on a wall console — preparing a route-update — and finds a short annotation in Veraine's hand on a fragment of pre-Ruusan Weave-theoretical writing. Per W2 evidence-of-passage: a few lines, marginal, no audience, her working-mind voice. She has been to this outpost. She has read the same fragment the outpost's own curators read, and she has noted — without rhetoric — a specific structural reading of it that is not the Order's. Ben registers the register more than the content: intellectually calm, precise, curious, inhumanly composed. He files it. He does not yet put it next to Kael's sentence. The reader does. Departure; close enough to feel the primary wound's pull on approach. H19 plants.

relationship_turns.to: genuine request — 'What is your plan, Skywalker?' is the chapter's most important line from her. She has moved her hand from Gavran's orbit to Ben's. Her arc moment of truth landed

relationship_turns.from: stranger from a thousand years ago
relationship_turns.to: compassionate operator — his warmth with the suffering Knight is genuine; his use of her as argument is also real. The two coexist. He is not a monster yet. He may never be

naming the problem — Kael's 'design problem' observation is the most work his voice has done in the book. His arc moment of truth landed. The fact that he does not know he has said the answer is the point

relationship_turns.from: direct contact closed (Ch 16); evidence-of-passage via ledger (Ch 17)
relationship_turns.to: mind-at-the-source — Ben now holds a second piece of Veraine's working mind, this one placed against the same primary material her opponents' successors are trying to read. The register is continuous with the Ch 17 ledger; the object is different. Per W2, this is evidence-of-passage beat 2 of five

exit_vector: The Steady Returns lifting from the outpost, course set direct to Veranthos. The primary wound's pull visible in the sensor fields — immense, gravitational. The young Knights behind them in a compound whose contemplative practices will not function again until the seal is mended. Ben with three sentences he did not have an hour ago: Sera's request, Kael's observation, Veraine's annotation. The resonance note one scroll away. The reader feels the pattern converging; Ben still does not.
notes: The book's lived_galaxy_texture obligation lands hardest in this chapter — the modern Jedi outpost is where cosmic stakes acquire faces. Three young Knights with specific disoriented gestures (too-still hands, a meditation drill abandoned mid-breath, a disciplined-senior who has built his identity on contemplation and can no longer do it) should appear. They are Ben's peers; they are not named at length but each is specific. Torin's compassion-as-weapon in s2 is the most dangerous ethical manoeuvre in his arc — the warmth must remain real, the calculation must remain visible over the head of the person he is touching. Sera's line 'What is your plan, Skywalker?' is a chapter anchor; deliver once and leave. Kael's 'design problem' observation is the other. Both are small lines doing immense work. Per W2 evidence-of-passage beat 2: Veraine's outpost-archive annotation is brief, lateral, unsigned — a marginal note on a pre-Ruusan fragment. She writes for herself. No performance. No rhetorical flourish. Her voice is continuous with the Ch 17 ledger register (precise, certain, intellectually restless, minimal affect). The beat sits in one scene (s3) and is carried as a sensory_details / action_beat, not as a lecture. The chapter's convergence is architectural: Kael's articulated critique and Veraine's archival trace are in the same physical location, at the same moment, registered by the same Ben. Voice: Zahn-empathy in s1 (the failing Knights); dialogue-drama precision in s2; Allston-understatement for Kael in s3. ANTI-PATTERNS: (a) do not have Ben recognise Kael's observation as the resonance answer on-page — the reader recognises it; Ben does not yet; (b) Torin's compassion must not tip into parody — the scene fails if he is obviously manipulating; (c) the outpost Knights are not named-and-characterised at length; they are specific faces and specific failings, nothing more; (d) per W2 anti-pattern, Veraine's annotation is not addressed to any reader — no taunt, no 'if you are reading this' framing; her ledger register does not warm or sharpen because Ben is the one now holding it; (e) per W2, Ben does not articulate on-page that the annotation means Veraine has been here before them; he registers a date, a hand, a register — that is enough.
